title: Quilltap Export Format — NDJSON stream (qtap-ndjson v1)
description:
Schema for a single line of a streaming .qtap export. A streaming .qtap file is newline-delimited JSON: the first line is an __envelope__ record carrying the manifest, the last line is an optional __footer__ carrying authoritative counts, and every line between is one tagged entity record. Validate each line against this schema individually — the file as a whole is not a JSON document.

Detection rule: a .qtap file whose first parseable JSON value is an object with format === 'qtap-ndjson' is streaming NDJSON. Anything else is the legacy monolithic {manifest, data} format described by qtap-export.schema.json.

Which record kinds appear depends on manifest.exportType. Records are emitted in dependency order: a parent always precedes its children (character before its wardrobe_item records, chat before its chat_message records, doc_mount_blob before its chunks), so a reader can resolve references without buffering the whole stream.

From 4.8 the document-store kinds (doc_mount_point, doc_mount_folder, doc_mount_document, doc_mount_blob and its chunks) are NOT exclusive to exportType 'document-stores': a 'characters' stream carries each character's vault the same way, emitted after that character's character_plugin_data records and before its memory records. A reader that keys doc-store handling off exportType rather than off the record kind will silently drop a character's photographs, correspondence and avatar. project_doc_mount_link never appears in a characters stream — a character vault has no project links.

RecordKind.description: Discriminator for the record. A reader that meets an unrecognised kind warns and skips it — that is how the format tolerates archives written by a newer build. An unrecognised manifest.exportType, by contrast, is fatal: a reader that does not know the type cannot assemble the payload.

Envelope.description: Always the first line. Its manifest.counts are best-effort and are usually empty for streaming exports; the footer carries the authoritative counts.

version.description: Stream format version. Adding new record kinds does not bump this.

Footer.description: Optional final line carrying the record counts actually emitted, so a reader can tell a complete stream from a truncated one.

SimpleRecord.description: One entity per line, payload in `data`. Parent references inside `data` use the exporting instance's IDs and are remapped at import time.

data.description: The entity, in the same shape the legacy monolithic format uses for its corresponding array element — with two exceptions that exist because the stream splits large payloads: a `character` carries no wardrobeItems or pluginData (those stream as their own records), and a `chat` carries no messages (likewise). A `memory` never carries an embedding at all; see the Memory definition in qtap-export.schema.json.

CharacterChildRecord.description: A wardrobe item or plugin-data blob belonging to the most recent `character` record. Split out so a large wardrobe cannot blow past the per-line size ceiling.

ChatChildRecord.description: A message, Inform row, annotation, or Document-Mode pane record belonging to the most recent `chat` record. Messages are split out so a chat with tens of thousands of them still streams; informs, annotations and chat documents follow the messages so a reader can resolve recordMessageId / consumedByMessageId / sourceMessageId against IDs it has already seen.

DocMountBlobRecord.description: Document-store blob header, emitted once before its byte chunks. NOTE: despite the name, doc_mount_blob_chunk has nothing to do with embeddings — it is the base64 splitting of binary blob content. The embedding table (doc_mount_chunks) is never exported at all.

data.description: Everything in ExportedDocumentStoreBlob except dataBase64, plus chunkCount.

DocMountBlobChunkRecord.description: One ordered slice of a document-store blob, keyed to its header by (mountPointId, sha256). Raw slices are 3 MiB — a multiple of 3 — so each base64 piece is padding-free and the reader can concatenate the encoded strings directly.

FileBlobRecord.description: General-library file byte header, emitted once after its `file` record and before its chunks. Absent when the file's bytes could not be read — the `file` record then carries _bytesMissing.

FileBlobChunkRecord.description: One ordered slice of a general-library file's bytes, keyed to its header by fileId. Same 3 MiB multiple-of-3 rule as the document-store chunks.
